target.label: mid-size TypeScript SaaS web application (payments, background jobs, third-party data acquisition, public scoring surface)

notes: Fourth run against this target class and the first on suite 1.74.0, under the identical configuration of the 2026-08-09 row (strong lead over strong operatives), so the suite version is what moved. Deltas: dispatches 22 to 21, findings 126 to 74, CONFIRMED 49 to 28 (ratio 0.39 to 0.38), covered negatives 176 to 164, highs 24 to 4, paneled 18 of 18 to 4 of 4 with survival 0.89 to 1.00, operative tokens roughly 2.98M to 2.59M, CONFIRMED per 100k 1.65 to 1.08; atlas 11 sections all consumed fresh with 1 falsified. First run in the store to carry a host line. **The suite’s version 4 orchestration machinery cannot run under the protocol’s own strong-lead configuration (L-043)**: the run contract compiler refuses any lead below frontier and the security campaign checker requires that contract, so the pre-registered strong-lead arms are unrunnable. Runtime artifacts must be git-ignored while placement expects the tracked vault runs folder (L-044). The anchor revalidator flagged 20 of the first 30 entries while a lead exact check found every anchor fresh: its path grammar admits no square brackets or spaces (L-045) and bare-filename masking recurred (L-027). An atlas section read fresh while wrong about counts evidenced by paths outside its own scope (L-046). **Panels again refined more than they killed (L-034)**: of four highs, one was promoted to confirmed on a panelist-built execution probe stronger than the finder’s, one had its cost corrected downward by half, and one mock-bounded confirmed high was cut two severity levels by an intent-lens panel, so a mock-bounded repro should not exempt a high (L-047). The operative tier rule held for single findings but recurred at chain level (L-020). Finished reviewers left test runners alive unseen by ledger or shape gate (L-048). A dirty target forced a committed-state worktree snapshot on a short path, with no skill guidance (L-049). Unparseable host background output forced the lead to re-emit every report (L-050). Fourteen prior fixes observed holding and recorded as verified-in edges.
